thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High tail latency and increased 503s on dedicated-pool-3. Autoscaler failing to add burst nodes. Paging on-call team. monitor: https://grafana/redwood/d/pool/dedicated-pool-3
Maria Chen: seeing the alert — confirmed spike in queue length and token backlog. Lots of customers hitting Dedicated. 503s start ~ 2105001200 UTC.
Jon Patel: on it. grabbing metrics + pool status.
Jon Patel: run: `rictl pools describe dedicated-pool-3`
Jon Patel: output:
```
name: dedicated-pool-3
status: degraded
nodes: 12 (max=12)
burst_capacity: disabled
autoscale: enabled
pending_queue_length: 420
avg_latency_p95: 480ms
```
Jon Patel: autoscaler hit max nodes and burst_capacity is disabled — looks like we never allowed burst in this pool config.
Sasha Roy: oof. any chance we can flip burst on quickly?
Alex Gomez: we have a toggle but need to be careful — toggle will spin up preemptible/burst nodes; could increase cost but should drop queues.
Priya Kapoor: also consider immediate rate limiting for non-SLA customers + disable async-heavy endpoints (batch embeddings) to free capacity.
Maria Chen: customer-impact check: 7 active Dedicated customers on this pool. Two high-priority customers seeing >25% error rate (429/503). Notifying account teams.
Jon Patel: plan: 1) enable burst_capacity on dedicated-pool-3 2) temporarily reduce per-route `max_concurrency` for non-protected routes 3) route heavy workloads to hosted fallback for low-tier customers 4) monitor and rollback if errors increase.
Maria Chen: agree. assign actions: @Alex enable burst, @Sasha apply rate limit rules, @Priya validate routing rules. I'll coordinate comms.
Alex Gomez: running command to enable burst:
```
rictl pools update dedicated-pool-3 --set burst_capacity=enabled --set burst_node_type=preemptible-nvidia-t4
```
Alex Gomez: Submitted. api returned job id `job-98321`. Expect nodes to begin provisioning in ~90-150s.
incident-bot: Job job-98321 started: provisioning burst nodes for dedicated-pool-3.
Sasha Roy: applying temporary rate limit for non-SLA routes (30 req/min)
Sasha Roy: command:
```
rictl routes update --pool dedicated-pool-3 --selector "tier!=sso_protected" --set rate_limit=30/m
```
Sasha Roy: applied. will take ~10s to propagate.
Priya Kapoor: kicking routing fallback: tagged low-tier customers to route to hosted-fallback cluster. Command:
```
rictl routing set-fallback --pool dedicated-pool-3 --selector "customer_tier=low" --fallback hosted-fallback-eu
```
Priya Kapoor: done.
Jon Patel: watching metrics. queue dropping from 420 -> 120 over last 3m. p95 latency 480ms -> 220ms.
Alex Gomez: burst nodes in; node count now 18 (12 reserved + 6 burst).
incident-bot: Job job-98321 completed: 6 burst nodes added to dedicated-pool-3.
Maria Chen: good. errors dropped to ~3% for affected customers, still seeing some 429s.
Sasha Roy: reduced `max_concurrency` on inference route for non-protected: `max_concurrency=2` via: `rictl routes update --pool dedicated-pool-3 --selector "tier!=sso_protected" --set max_concurrency=2`
Jon Patel: 429 rate decreased. throughput stable.
Priya Kapoor: note — one large customer was running long-running batched embeddings; we throttled their queued jobs and routed smaller requests to hosted-fallback. They noticed degraded throughput; account notified.
Maria Chen: customer-impact summary so far: 7 customers affected, 2 high-priority (25% peak error -> back to ~3%), incident start 2105001200, mitigation started 2105001260, primary mitigation effective by 2105001340.
Jon Patel: I'm going to hand off to Maria for overnight watch. I've got another page in 30m.
Jon Patel: @Maria thanks — please follow the runbook section "Dedicated pool burst toggle" and document exact commands + timestamps.
Maria Chen: taking handoff. I'll keep watch and keep support informed.
incident-bot: oncall handover recorded: from Jon Patel to Maria Chen at 2105001405 UTC.
Alex Gomez: leaving note: we saw autoscaler hit the hard node cap (max=12). action item: increase autoscale max for pools with >5 customers or enable burst by default. filing follow-up ticket.
Sasha Roy: another quick action item: add alert for burst_capacity=false when pool customer_count>=3 and predicted_load>threshold. Right now alert only fires on queue length.
Priya Kapoor: follow-up prod task: create a traffic-class policy to automatically route low-priority workloads to hosted fallback when queue length > 200.
Maria Chen: ack. support update: posted to #customer-impact with list of affected accounts and mitigation steps. CC: sales & CSMs.
Maria Chen: final note for postmortem: why was burst disabled on this pool? who changed default? Need audit. Also check why autoscaler didn't increase earlier — maybe bounds too tight.
Jon Patel: add perf tweak: consider faster prewarm for burst nodes to reduce provisioning time (target <60s).
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (burst enabled, rate limits, routing fallback). Customer errors reduced. Next: postmortem assigned to eng-platform + devex.
Maria Chen: closing oncall thread; will open a postmortem issue with timeline. leaving monitoring alerts at reduced thresholds. :white_check_mark:
Sasha Roy: nice work team :thumbsup:
Alex Gomez: filed ticket: #PLAT-4579 titled "Enable burst by default for multi-customer Dedicated pools + autoscale bounds review"
Priya Kapoor: adding runbook improvement: include explicit rollback steps for burst toggle (how to safely drain burst nodes).
Maria Chen: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with customer comms drafts in #customer-impact.
